acceptanceCriteria: [unit] legacyRoleForRoleKey from apps/api/src/permissions/legacy-project-roles.ts returns 'ADMIN' for project-admin, 'DEVELOPER' for developer, and 'VIEWER' for each of viewer, reviewer and qa-lead.

[integration] For a user with a legacy ProjectMember row of role VIEWER in p1 and a project-admin binding in p1, userProjectRole(prisma.client, <user id>, p1) resolves 'ADMIN'.

[integration] For an agent with a legacy AgentProject row in p1, a viewer binding in p2, and a viewer binding in a soft-deleted project p3, accessibleProjectIds(prisma.client, { type: 'AGENT', id: <agent id> }) resolves exactly [p1, p2] in ascending order.
[integration] For a user with a projectId-null developer binding, accessibleProjectIds(prisma.client, { type: 'USER', id: <user id> }) resolves the ids of every non-deleted project.

[integration] principalIdsWithAccess(prisma.client, p1, 'USER') resolves exactly the ids of a user with a legacy row in p1, a user with a binding in p1, and a user with a projectId-null viewer binding. [integration] For an agent with a legacy AgentProject row in p1 (createdAt t1, addedById u1) and a later viewer binding in p1, listProjectMemberships(prisma.client, p1, 'AGENT') returns one entry for it with since t1, addedByUserId u1 and role 'VIEWER', and returns no entry for an agent whose only binding is projectId-null.

[integration] In p1, with user a holding a legacy ADMIN row, user b holding a project-admin binding, user c holding both, and disabled user d holding a project-admin binding, countActiveProjectAdmins(prisma.client, p1) resolves 3.

[integration] For a user with developer and reviewer bindings in p1, a developer binding in p2 and a legacy row in p1, MembershipService.removeProjectBindings({ type: 'USER', id: <user id> }, p1, ['developer']) resolves 1. Afterwards the user still holds the reviewer binding in p1, the developer binding in p2 and the legacy row.

[integration] For a user whose only source in p1 is a developer binding, after PermissionService.can(<user principal>, 'ticket.create', { projectId: p1 }) answered allowed true, MembershipService.removeProjectBindings({ type: 'USER', id: <user id> }, p1) makes the next identical can call answer allowed false.

routing.reasoning: A shared multi-source persistence abstraction adds role precedence, source provenance and cache-aware deletion. Access-control code requires isolated TDD; algorithms and interfaces are sufficiently specified for standard multi-file backend implementation.

userStories.title: Project access and project lists read bindings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make project access, project lists and home projects read binding and legacy access sources.

**Motivation** — A user bound to `developer` in a project through `/role-bindings` is still refused by that project's routes, because `ProjectAccessService.resolveMembership` reads only `ProjectMember`.

**Approach** — Each row keeps the method's name, parameters and return type.

| Reader | Today reads | Target |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `PrismaProjectRepository.findMembershipRole(projectId, userId)` | `ProjectMember.role` | `userProjectRole` |
| `PrismaProjectRepository.isAgentOnRoster(projectId, agentId)` | `AgentProject` row | `agentHasProjectAccess` |
| `PrismaProjectRepository.findAllForUser(userId)`, `findAllForAgent(agentId)` | `members` / `agents: { some }` | non-deleted projects whose id is in `accessibleProjectIds` |
| `PrismaHomeRepository.findProjects(caller)` (non-admin) | `members: { some }` | `id` in `accessibleProjectIds({ type: 'USER', id: caller.id })` |

Legacy repository methods keep their names, parameters and return types. Only what they read changes. Their callers, and the specs that stub them, are unaffected. `permissions-p1-cleanup` deletes the queries file together with these methods.

Global admins are unchanged. Global `owner` and `admin` bindings are mirrored into `User.role = 'ADMIN'` by `permissions-p1-roles`, and every reader keeps its existing `User.role === 'ADMIN'` / `principal.role === 'ADMIN'` short-cut. GLOBAL-scope roles are never a membership source (see Sources).

These are access-source reads: legacy membership plus PROJECT-scope bindings in the project and projectId-null PROJECT bindings. Binding roles map project-admin to ADMIN, developer to DEVELOPER, all other keys to VIEWER; legacy role strings remain unchanged. Pass this.prisma.client first to join transactions and do not cache. Preserve non-deleted project filtering, home name order and scoping-off agents receiving all projects. ProjectAccessService, ProjectsService and HomeService remain unchanged, as do agentRoles, AgentAuthProvider and CASL. Existing project-access/guard/projects service mocks retain signatures; projects-brief.routes.spec.ts uses a global-admin path and does not reach these membership reads. Keep legacy-row DB regressions.

**Scope** — In: four project-repository reads and the home non-admin predicate, with binding-only HTTP checks. Out: query implementation (US-001), ticket/fleet/notification readers (US-003..US-005), member/invite/roster writes (US-006/007), permission-key enforcement and agent role derivation.

**Interface** — Preserve existing signatures:
```ts
findMembershipRole(projectId: string, userId: string): Promise<string | null>;
isAgentOnRoster(projectId: string, agentId: string): Promise<boolean>;
findAllForUser(userId: string): Promise<ProjectDomain[]>;
findAllForAgent(agentId: string): Promise<ProjectDomain[]>;
findProjects(caller: HomeCaller): Promise<HomeProjectRow[]>;
```

userStories.title: Ticket assignment, assignee search and the domain writer read bindings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make assignment eligibility, assignee search and domain-writer user-role provenance read the compatibility union.

**Motivation** — This feature closes the gap from both sides: readers see bindings, and the routes that grant membership write bindings.

**Approach** — Each row keeps the method's name, parameters and return type.

| Reader | Today reads | Target |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `PrismaTicketsRepository.findProjectMemberRole(projectId, userId)` | `ProjectMember.role` | `userProjectRole` |
| `PrismaTicketsRepository.isAgentOnProjectRoster(projectId, agentId)` | `AgentProject` row | `agentHasProjectAccess` (still called under `lockProjectAgents`) |
| `PrismaProjectAssigneesRepository.search(projectId, q, limit)` | `ProjectMember` and `AgentProject` | users and agents whose id is in `principalIdsWithAccess`, with the same filters (enabled users, assignable agent statuses, `q`), order and `limit` |
| `PrismaKodaDomainWriterRepository.findUserProjectRoles(projectId, userId)` | `User.role` and `ProjectMember.role` | the same two entries as today (`'ADMIN'` when `User.role` is `'ADMIN'`, and the legacy row's raw role), plus `userProjectRole` when non-null, de-duplicated. Keeping the raw legacy role means a legacy `AGENT` row still satisfies the writer's allowed roles when a `viewer` binding outranks it in `strongestProjectRole` |

Legacy repository methods keep their names, parameters and return types. Only what they read changes. Their callers, and the specs that stub them, are unaffected. `permissions-p1-cleanup` deletes the queries file together with these methods.

Use access sources, including projectId-null PROJECT bindings, never GLOBAL roles. Pass this.prisma.client first, retain transaction participation and no caching. Keep user/global ADMIN shortcuts and ticket assignment under the roster advisory lock. Assignee search retains enabled users, ACTIVE/PAUSED agents, plain case-insensitive substring q, name/id ordering, user name fallback to email, users-before-agents and combined limit. Keep raw legacy writer roles separately before adding the strongest compatibility role: legacy AGENT plus viewer binding returns both AGENT and VIEWER. Agent actors still trigger no user membership reads. TicketsService, ProjectAssigneesService and KodaDomainWriter are unchanged.

Update prisma-project-assignees.repository.spec.ts mocks to drive roleBinding/projectMember/agentProject queries. Update test/unit/koda-domain-writer/find-user-project-roles.spec.ts and koda-domain-writer-role-provenance.spec.ts with binding reads, preserving global ADMIN and agent no-read assertions. Update test/integration/events/event-write-operations.integration.spec.ts mocked membership reads without changing event assertions. PG tests enter through assign/assignees routes and KodaDomainWriter.writeTicketEvent. Use an already authorized global-admin HTTP caller to isolate the binding-only assignee's eligibility without requiring US-002; the writer case instead uses the stated binding-only user actor. Agent fixture work roles still come from AgentRoleEntry, not from the viewer access binding.

**Scope** — In: two ticket-repository checks, assignee search, writer roles and associated tests. Out: project access/list adoption (US-002), fleet/notification readers (US-004/005), route membership writes (US-006/007), changing CASL or writer allowed-role policy.

**Interface** — Preserve existing signatures:
```ts
findProjectMemberRole(projectId: string, userId: string): Promise<string | null>;
isAgentOnProjectRoster(projectId: string, agentId: string): Promise<boolean>;
search(projectId: string, q: string, limit: number): Promise<AssigneeDomain[]>;
findUserProjectRoles(projectId: string, userId: string): Promise<string[]>;
```
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] POST /projects/p1/tickets/<ref>/assign with { userId } for an enabled user whose only source in p1 is a developer binding answers 200, and the ticket's assignedToUserId is that user.
[integration] POST /projects/p1/tickets/<ref>/assign with { userId } for an enabled non-admin user with no source in p1 answers 403.
[integration] POST /projects/p1/tickets/<ref>/assign with { agentId } for an ACTIVE agent whose only source in p1 is a viewer binding answers 200, and the ticket's assignedToAgentId is that agent.
[integration] POST /projects/p1/tickets/<ref>/assign with { agentId } for an ACTIVE agent with no source in p1 answers 409 with error code tickets.agentNotInProject.

[integration] GET /projects/p1/assignees returns, among its items, a type: 'user' item for an enabled user whose only source in p1 is a developer binding, and a type: 'agent' item for an ACTIVE agent whose only source in p1 is a viewer binding.

[integration] GET /projects/p1/assignees returns a type: 'user' item for an enabled user whose only source is a projectId-null viewer binding, and no item for a disabled user whose only source in p1 is a developer binding.
[integration] GET /projects/p1/assignees returns a type: 'user' item for an enabled user whose only source in p1 is a legacy ProjectMember row.
[integration] KodaDomainWriter.writeTicketEvent with a user actor whose only source in p1 is a developer binding records the ticket event and answers its canonicalId.
[integration] KodaDomainWriter.writeTicketEvent with a user actor whose only source in p1 is a viewer binding rejects with ForbiddenAppException and records no event.

routing.reasoning: Three consumer modules and query-sensitive doubles must preserve assignment locking, search semantics and legacy authorization provenance. Access-control changes require isolated TDD; interfaces and transformations are explicit.

The replacing invariant: the stubs drive the compatibility queries (roleBinding, projectMember and agentProject reads) instead, and search keeps its filters, its users-then-agents order and its limit.

The replacing invariant: findUserProjectRoles still answers ['ADMIN'] for a global admin and the legacy row's role, plus the user's userProjectRole when non-null, de-duplicated, with the binding reads stubbed too; a user with a legacy AGENT row and a viewer binding answers both 'AGENT' and 'VIEWER'.

its Prisma mock stubs projectMember only. The replacing invariant: the mock also answers the binding reads the queries make; event assertions are unchanged.

userStories.title: Fleet activity scoping and schedule owners read bindings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Include binding-derived access in fleet activity scope and schedule owner access without changing fleet policies.

**Motivation** — This feature closes the gap from both sides: readers see bindings, and the routes that grant membership write bindings.

**Approach** — Each row keeps the method's name, parameters and return type.

| Reader | Today reads | Target |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `PrismaFleetActivityRepository.findMemberProjectIds(userId)` | `ProjectMember` | `accessibleProjectIds({ type: 'USER', id: userId })` |
| `PrismaScheduleRepository.findOwnerAccess(projectId, userId)` | `projectRole` from `ProjectMember` | `projectRole` from `userProjectRole` |

Legacy repository methods keep their names, parameters and return types. Only what they read changes. Their callers, and the specs that stub them, are unaffected. `permissions-p1-cleanup` deletes the queries file together with these methods.

Global admins are unchanged. Global `owner` and `admin` bindings are mirrored into `User.role = 'ADMIN'` by `permissions-p1-roles`, and every reader keeps its existing `User.role === 'ADMIN'` / `principal.role === 'ADMIN'` short-cut. GLOBAL-scope roles are never a membership source (see Sources).

Pass this.prisma.client first. Access sources combine legacy membership, local PROJECT bindings and projectId-null PROJECT bindings; global project grants expand to all non-deleted projects. Preserve owner existence, disabled and globalRole fields and replace projectRole only. FleetActivityService, SchedulesService, ScheduleTicker and mayDispatch are unchanged. Developer owners retain dispatch rights; viewer-only owners do not gain authority. No query caching. Existing fleet-activity.service.spec.ts, approvals.service.spec.ts, schedules.service.spec.ts and schedule-ticker.spec.ts boundary doubles remain unchanged. fleet-schedule-repository.integration.spec.ts retains legacy-row fixtures. PG tests exercise activity/counts visibility, schedule enable and real ticker dispatch/no-dispatch entry points. For schedule-enable cases use an already authorized global-admin caller distinct from the binding-only schedule owner, so owner-role validation does not require US-002. Activity and approval-count tests must retain the stated non-admin binding-only caller. Retain the unchanged viewer-owner rejection from mayDispatch as a regression assertion.

**Scope** — In: activity project ids and schedule owner repository role plus integration behavior. Out: query implementation (US-001), project access (US-002), ticket/notification readers (US-003/005), membership/roster writes (US-006/007), scheduling algorithms, state transitions and fleet permission-key enforcement.

**Interface** — Preserve existing signatures:
```ts
findMemberProjectIds(userId: string): Promise<string[]>;
findOwnerAccess(projectId: string, userId: string): Promise<OwnerAccess>;
```
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] For a non-admin user whose only source in p1 is a developer binding and who has no source in p2, GET /fleet/activity returns the activity rows of p1 and none of p2.
[integration] For a non-admin user whose only source in p1 is a developer binding and who has no source in p2, GET /fleet/approval-counts counts p1's pending approvals and not p2's.
[integration] POST /projects/p1/fleet/schedules/<id>/enable for a disabled schedule whose owner's only source in p1 is a developer binding answers 200, and the schedule is enabled.

[integration] POST /projects/p1/fleet/schedules/<id>/enable for a disabled schedule whose owner's only source in p1 is a viewer binding answers 409 with error code fleet.scheduleOwnerNoAccess, preserving the existing schedule-owner role restriction.
[integration] A ScheduleTicker tick over a due schedule whose owner's only source in p1 is a developer binding dispatches a job for the schedule.
[integration] A ScheduleTicker tick over a due schedule whose owner's only source in p1 is a viewer binding dispatches no job and disables the schedule with reason owner_lost_access.

routing.reasoning: Two repository substitutions reuse defined query/policy boundaries. Activity visibility and schedule-owner authorization require isolated security TDD.

userStories.title: Notifications, mentions and the member-added email read bindings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Recognize binding-derived access in notification eligibility, mentions and MEMBER_ADDED email content.

**Motivation** — This feature closes the gap from both sides: readers see bindings, and the routes that grant membership write bindings.

**Approach** — Each row keeps the method's name, parameters and return type.

| Reader | Today reads | Target |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `NotificationEligibility.filter` | `projectMember.findMany` | for each distinct `projectId` in the drafts, `principalIdsWithAccess(projectId, 'USER')` |
| `TicketMentionResolver.mentionedUserIds` | `projectMemberships: { some }` | enabled users that are global `ADMIN` or in `principalIdsWithAccess(projectId, 'USER')` |
| `EmailContentBuilder` (MEMBER_ADDED) | `projectMember.findUnique` | `userProjectRole`; `null` keeps `skip: 'SOURCE_GONE'`, otherwise it is the template's `role` |

The callers are persistence code. The queries are called from repositories, and from the three classes that already read Prisma directly (`NotificationEligibility`, `TicketMentionResolver`, `EmailContentBuilder`, tolerated legacy per `.nax/rules/api-data.md`). No service changes its constructor to read membership.

These readers use access sources: legacy rows and PROJECT-scope bindings both local and projectId-null, never GLOBAL-scope bindings. Pass this.prisma.client first; do not cache. Keep enabled global ADMIN eligibility via User.role. Notification eligibility still excludes the actor and disabled/unknown users and preserves projectless draft behavior. Mentions still follow parsed text order and exclude disabled users. Email retains missing/disabled-user and missing/deleted-project handling, role data and URL generation; null access role skips SOURCE_GONE.

Altitude note, verbatim: US-005 enters at `NotificationWriter.deliver` (the only notification insert path), `EmailContentBuilder.build` (what the email processor calls per row) and `TicketMentionResolver.mentionedUserIds` (whose ticket subscriber callers are unchanged).

Update notification-eligibility.spec.ts to drive compatibility reads while preserving recipient filtering assertions; update ticket-mention.resolver.spec.ts membership reads while retaining global ADMIN/text order; update email-content.builder.spec.ts role reads while retaining no-source SOURCE_GONE. Keep legacy-row notification/email integration fixtures.

**Scope** — In: three tolerated direct-Prisma consumers, affected mocks and entry-point PG tests. Out: queries (US-001), repository consumers (US-002..US-004), membership/roster writes (US-006/007), changing notification production/preferences, email processing or mention parsing.

**Interface** — Preserve filter, mentionedUserIds and build names, parameters and return types. Query signatures are verbatim:
```ts
export function principalIdsWithAccess(db: PrismaClient, projectId: string, type: PrincipalType): Promise<string[]>;
export function userProjectRole(db: PrismaClient, userId: string, projectId: string): Promise<string | null>;
```
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] NotificationWriter.deliver with a draft for project p1 addressed to an enabled user whose only source in p1 is a developer binding inserts a Notification row for that user.

[integration] NotificationWriter.deliver with drafts for project p1 inserts no Notification row for an enabled non-admin user with no source in p1, and inserts one for an enabled global ADMIN user with no source in p1.
[integration] NotificationWriter.deliver with a draft for project p1 addressed to an enabled user whose only source is a projectId-null viewer binding inserts a Notification row for that user.
[integration] TicketMentionResolver.mentionedUserIds(p1, text), where text mentions an enabled user whose only source in p1 is a developer binding, returns that user's id.
[integration] TicketMentionResolver.mentionedUserIds(p1, text), where text mentions an enabled non-admin user with no source in p1, returns an empty list.
[integration] EmailContentBuilder.build of a MEMBER_ADDED email row for a user whose only source in p1 is a developer binding answers template data whose role is 'DEVELOPER'.
[integration] EmailContentBuilder.build of a MEMBER_ADDED email row for a user with no source in p1 answers skip 'SOURCE_GONE'.

routing.reasoning: Three existing consumers adopt specified query functions while retaining filtering/content semantics. Recipient access eligibility requires the security override.

modifiedFiles.reason: it stubs prisma.client.projectMember.findMany to decide membership. The replacing invariant: the stubs answer the compatibility queries' reads instead, and the asserted filtering (never the actor, never disabled or unknown users, members or global admins only for project drafts) is unchanged.

it stubs user.findMany with a projectMemberships filter. The replacing invariant: membership comes from the compatibility queries' reads, global ADMINs still pass, and the result keeps the text's order.
it stubs projectMember.findUnique for MEMBER_ADDED. The replacing invariant: the role comes from the compatibility queries' reads, and no source still skips with SOURCE_GONE.

userStories.title: Member and invite routes write bindings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make member and invite writes create bindings while local membership pages, duplicate checks and admin protection read the union.

**Motivation** — This feature closes the gap from both sides: readers see bindings, and the routes that grant membership write bindings.

**Approach** — All routes keep their paths, request DTOs, response DTOs, status codes and error codes. The OpenAPI contract does not change.

**Members** (`ProjectMembersService`, `/projects/:slug/members`). Each write runs inside `membership.afterCommit(() => txManager.run(...))` and takes the existing `lockMembers(projectId)` advisory lock first.
- **Repository reads.** `PrismaProjectMembersRepository.findMemberPage(projectId, page)` builds the page from `listProjectMemberships(db, projectId, 'USER')`, joined with each user's `email`, `name` and `disabled`, and sliced by `IPageOption`; `role` is the membership's `role`, `joinedAt` its `since`, and `total` counts the memberships. `findMember(projectId, userId)` answers the user's record when `localProjectRole` is non-null (with that role and the membership's `since`), else `null`. `countProjectAdmins(projectId)` answers `countActiveProjectAdmins`. A new `deleteMemberIfPresent(projectId, userId)` deletes the legacy row when there is one.
- **List.** Unchanged in the service: the page from `findMemberPage`, `canManage` and `viewerRole` from `resolveMembership`.
- **Add.** After the existing user lookups, a user for whom `findMember` answers a record gets 409 `members`. Otherwise the service creates a binding of `ROLE_KEY_FOR_LEGACY_ROLE[dto.role ?? 'VIEWER']` in the project. The response is the new member, as `findMember` answers it.
- **Update role.** A user for whom `findMember` answers `null` gets 404 `members`. The last-admin rule keeps its meaning: the change is refused with 409 `members.lastAdmin` when the user's current role is `ADMIN`, the user is not disabled, the new role is not `ADMIN`, the caller is not a global admin, and `countProjectAdmins` is at most 1. Otherwise the service calls `removeProjectBindings(user, projectId, ['project-admin', 'developer', 'viewer'])`, `deleteMemberIfPresent`, and creates the binding for the new role. Other project bindings (for example `reviewer`) are kept. The response is the member as `findMember` answers it after the write. Because the old binding is replaced, the member's `joinedAt` (`since`) becomes the new binding's `createdAt` unless another local source is older; this re-dating is accepted.
- **Remove.** A user for whom `findMember` answers `null` gets 404 `members`. The same last-admin rule applies with no new role. Otherwise the service calls `removeProjectBindings(user, projectId)` and `deleteMemberIfPresent`.

**Invites.**
- `ProjectInvitesService.addExistingUser(projectId, userId, role, principal)` gains the calling principal, for the granter (its caller `create` already has it). Inside its transaction it first takes the project members lock (a new `PrismaProjectInvitesMembersRepository.lockMembers(projectId)`, the same `lockProjectMembers` advisory lock `ProjectMembersService` takes), then checks: a user whose `localProjectRole` is non-null answers 409 `invites.memberExists`. Otherwise it creates a binding of `ROLE_KEY_FOR_LEGACY_ROLE[role]` instead of a `ProjectMember` row. The ADDED response's `member` is built from the user's `email` and `name` (`PrismaProjectInvitesMembersRepository.findUserState` also returns `name`), `role` is the mapped legacy role, `joinedAt` the created binding's `createdAt`, and `disabled` false. The MEMBER_ADDED schedule stays in the same transaction, and the transaction runs inside `membership.afterCommit`. The local check goes through a new `PrismaProjectInvitesMembersRepository.findLocalRole(projectId, userId)`.
- `InviteAcceptanceService.accept`: inside the existing transaction, after creating the user, it creates a binding of `ROLE_KEY_FOR_LEGACY_ROLE[invite.role]` in the invite's project and calls `membership.bindBaseline({ type: 'USER', id })`, instead of creating a `ProjectMember` row. The transaction runs inside `membership.afterCommit`. A rejected acceptance writes no binding.

**Granter.** A route write records the calling user: `{ type: 'USER', id: principal.id }`. These routes already refuse agents (`assertProjectAdmin`). An invite acceptance records `{ type: 'SYSTEM', id: 'invite' }`.
**Constructor order.** A service that gains `MembershipService` takes it as a required parameter appended last (none of them has an `@Optional()` parameter).

Local membership means the legacy row plus project-specific PROJECT bindings, not projectId-null grants. GLOBAL-scope roles never supply membership. Use this.prisma.client through repository helpers so all reads/writes and schedules join the caller transaction. The shared member lock serializes direct member and invite adds; do not rely on createBinding idempotence to distinguish duplicates. Two concurrent existing-user invite adds leave one binding and one MEMBER_ADDED schedule when email is configured. Keep user lookup/disabled errors, last-admin behavior and accepted re-dating. Keep acceptance token claims, bcrypt outside the transaction and session issuance after commit. A rejected acceptance rolls back user/binding writes.

Modify project-members.service.spec.ts to pass membership fourth and expect mapped createBinding, removeProjectBindings and deleteMemberIfPresent; preserve last-admin/not-found assertions. project-members.module.spec.ts FakeGlobalsModule gains MembershipService. project-invites.service.spec.ts passes membership eighth and expects mapped createBinding/local-role conflict. invite-acceptance.service.spec.ts passes membership fifth and expects project grant plus bindBaseline. userStories.title: Agent roster routes and agent reach read and write bindings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Back the project agent roster with local compatibility membership and viewer writes while agent reach uses all access sources.

**Motivation** — This feature closes the gap from both sides: readers see bindings, and the routes that grant membership write bindings.

**Approach** — All routes keep their paths, request DTOs, response DTOs, status codes and error codes. The OpenAPI contract does not change.

**Agent roster** (`AgentsService`, `/projects/:slug/agents`). `AgentsService` already takes `MembershipService` (fourth constructor parameter). Writes keep the existing `lockProjectAgents(projectId)` lock and run inside `membership.afterCommit`.
- **List.** `PrismaAgentRepository.findProjectRoster(projectId)` keeps its return type and order (agent name ascending) and builds its rows from `listProjectMemberships(db, projectId, 'AGENT')`: `addedAt` is the membership's `since`, `addedById` its `addedByUserId`, and `addedByName` that user's name (or null). The agent fields and the open-ticket summary are computed as today.
- **Add** (`addToProject`). After the existing project, agent and OFFLINE checks, an agent with a local source (new `PrismaAgentRepository.hasLocalMembership(agentId, projectId)`, true when `localProjectRole` is non-null) answers 409 `projectAgents.alreadyAssigned`. Otherwise the service creates a `viewer` binding in the project, granted by the adding user. The response is the new row as `findProjectRoster` answers it.
- **Two readings, on purpose.** An agent whose only source is a global project binding passes the access checks (`isOnProjectRoster`, so pickup and `PATCH /projects/:slug/agents/:agentSlug`; `/agents/me`) but is not listed by `findProjectRoster` and cannot be removed through the roster route, which use local sources.
- **Remove** (`removeFromProject`). An agent without a local source (`hasLocalMembership` false) answers 404 `projectAgents`. The open-ticket refusal (409 `projectAgents.hasOpenTickets`) is unchanged. Otherwise the service calls `removeProjectBindings(agent, projectId)` and the existing `removeFromProjectRoster`, which deletes the legacy row if there is one.

Additional reader rows, verbatim:
| Reader | Today reads | Target |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `PrismaAgentRepository.isOnProjectRoster(agentId, projectId)` | `AgentProject` row | `agentHasProjectAccess`. Its callers are pickup (`suggestTicket`) and `isOnProjectRosterBySlug`; `removeFromProject` stops calling it (see Agent roster) |
| `PrismaAgentRepository.findRosterProjects(agentId)` | `AgentProject` | non-deleted projects whose id is in `accessibleProjectIds({ type: 'AGENT', id })`, ordered by slug |

The roster grants project access, as today. The agent's work rights inside the project still come from its global `AgentRoleEntry` roles until enforce-core. Local sources are legacy AgentProject plus project-specific PROJECT bindings; projectId-null PROJECT grants are access-only and GLOBAL roles are never membership. Pass this.prisma.client first so duplicate checks, binding changes, open-ticket checks, legacy deletion and response reads share txManager.run. Wrap the owning transaction with membership.afterCommit. Preserve lockProjectAgents before local check/write/re-read; idempotent createBinding alone must not make duplicate adds succeed. Granter is USER/addedById. Do not delete global project bindings. Preserve roles/capabilities and ticket summaries: exclude CLOSED/REJECTED/deleted tickets, retain total open count and oldest-first refs capped at 10. Added-by provenance comes from the earliest local source and a binding granter maps to a user only for grantedByType USER.

Existing endpoint.e2e.spec.ts roster cases assert viewer RoleBinding and grantedById, and refused DELETE retains it. Keep existing legacy roster repository integration tests; add a separate PG HTTP file for route ACs.

**Scope** — In: local roster read and access reach methods, hasLocalMembership, add/remove binding writes and related mocks/row assertions. Out: queries (US-001), project-access adoption (US-002), ticket/fleet/notification/member implementation (US-003..US-006), agentRoles/update-roles changes, deleting addToProjectRoster, DTO changes, new endpoint.e2e cases, cache commit-timing tests and assignment locking for DELETE /role-bindings/:id.

**Interface** — Preserve contracts and add local detection:
```ts
findProjectRoster(projectId: string): Promise<ProjectAgentRecord[]>;
isOnProjectRoster(agentId: string, projectId: string): Promise<boolean>;
findRosterProjects(agentId: string): Promise<{ slug: string; name: string }[]>;
hasLocalMembership(agentId: string, projectId: string): Promise<boolean>;
addToProject(projectSlug: string, agentSlug: string, addedById: string): Promise<ProjectAgentDto>;
removeFromProject(projectSlug: string, agentSlug: string): Promise<void>;
```

```ts
removeProjectBindings(principal: PrincipalRef, projectId: string, roleKeys?: readonly string[]): Promise<number>;
```
